_note: Long-term gains on equity shares bought and sold with securities transaction tax, and on equity-oriented fund and business-trust units sold with it, charged apart from total income (D-244). TY 2026-27: Income-tax Act, 2025 s.198(2)(a) (p.222): "income-tax calculated on such long-term capital gains exceeding ₹ 125000 at the rate of 12.5%". TY 2025-26: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.112A(2)(i)(b) as substituted by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 s.31 (pp.27–28): "exceeding one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees … at the rate of twelve and one-half per cent. for any transfer which takes place on or after the 23rd day of July, 2024". The ladder is applied to the gains after the basic-exemption shift (RATE-CG-SHORTFALL-ORDER): 1961 s.112A(2) proviso reduces them "for the purposes of clause (i)", and the Department's ITR-2 utility (AY 2026-27) shifts first and exempts after. TY 2026-27: s.198(3)(b) taxes the shifted balance "at the rate as referred to in sub-section (2)" — whether the Rs. 1,25,000 survives the shift is OQ-33; the declared default is that it does, as under the 1961 Act. Chapter VIII is kept off by s.198(6) / s.112A(5); the rebate under s.198(7) / s.112A(6) is W-089's. Sources: docs/taxplanning-build/sources/2026-10-18-capital-gains-basis.md rows 18–20.

introducedBy.instrumentCitation: Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 (15 of 2024), s.31 — Income-tax Act, 1961 s.112A(2)(i) (ten per cent. before 23-7-2024, twelve and one-half per cent. on or after, above one lakh twenty-five thousand rupees), deemed substituted w.e.f. 23-7-2024
